title: DSPM Data Classification Settings: synced DLP engines, the sensitivity setting and document categories

prose.label: Engines and dictionaries.
prose.text: {{engine-definition}} {{predefined-engines}} Only two engines are quoted {{gap:predefined-engine-list}}. {{uses-predefined}} The settings page lists Predefined or Custom engine types {{gap:predefined-or-custom}}.

prose.label: Document categories.
prose.text: {{document-categories}} Classification as a scan feature is in [[dspm.scanning:classification]].

checks.do: Whether a classification statement comes from the Understanding Data Classification page (predefined engines and dictionaries) or from the settings page (Predefined or Custom engine types).

engines-synced-from-zia.statement: DSPM classification uses DLP engines and dictionaries synced from Internet & SaaS (ZIA); the DLP engines can only be viewed in the Admin Console and can be modified in Internet & SaaS with the necessary permissions.

quotes: DSPM supports data classification by using robust DLP engines and dictionaries that are synced from Internet & SaaS (ZIA).
You can only view the DLP engines in the Zscaler Admin Console. You can modify a DLP engine in Internet & SaaS if you have the necessary permissions.

dspm-channel-filter.statement: Only DLP engines assigned to the DSPM channel in Internet & SaaS (ZIA) are displayed and available for selection in DSPM.

quotes: Only DLP engines assigned to the DSPM channel in Internet & SaaS (ZIA) are displayed and available for selection.

settings-columns.statement: The Data Classification Settings page lists synced engines with Engine Type (Predefined or Custom), Enabled (whether evaluation is enabled) and Sensitive (the sensitivity setting).

quotes: Engine Type: The type (Predefined or Custom) of DLP engine.
Enabled: Whether the DLP engine evaluation is enabled or not.
Sensitive: The data sensitivity setting (enabled or disabled) for the DLP engine.

sensitivity-default.statement: By default, the sensitivity setting is enabled for all DLP engines.

quotes: By default, the sensitivity setting is enabled for all DLP engines.

sensitivity-disable-all.statement: If the sensitivity setting is disabled for all DLP engines, any new engine added in Internet & SaaS is not automatically synced with DSPM and its sensitivity setting must be enabled manually in the Zscaler Admin Console.

quotes: If you disable the sensitivity setting for all DLP engines, any new DLP engine that is added to Internet & SaaS is not automatically synced with DSPM.
You need to manually enable the sensitivity settings for such DLP engines in the Zscaler Admin Console.

sensitivity-levels.statement: DSPM's documented examples of sensitivity: high for PII or credit card numbers, moderate for email addresses, low for data with nothing sensitive or confidential.

quotes: the sensitivity level is high for personally identifiable information (PII) or credit card numbers, moderate for email addresses, and low for data that does not have any sensitive or confidential information.

engine-definition.statement: A DLP engine is a collection of one or more DLP dictionaries, and the service provides predefined DLP engines and supports custom DLP engines.

quotes: A DLP engine is a security solution that comprises a collection of one or more DLP dictionaries.
The Zscaler service provides predefined DLP engines and supports custom DLP engines.

document-categories.statement: The DLP engine running in DSPM classifies each document with ML categories DMV, Financial, HR, Immigration, Insurance, Legal, Medical, Medical Imaging, Real Estate, Source Code and Technical, each with subcategories.

quotes: The DLP engine running in DSPM automatically classifies each document (file) using the following ML categories and subcategories:
| DMV | Vehicle Registration and Titling Documents
| Financial | Invoices and Expense Reports
| HR | Applicant and Employee Records
| Immigration | Citizenship and Naturalization Documents
| Insurance | Business Insurance Documents
| Legal | Miscellaneous Legal Documents
| Medical | Legal and Regulatory Documents
| Medical Imaging | Schematics Satellite Images ID Cards |
| Real Estate | Lease and Rental Documents
| Source Code | C C++ C# Dart Go HTML
| Technical | Technical Specifications and Design Documents

predefined-engines.statement: The predefined DLP engines page lists engines whose names end in predefined, e.g. Credit Cards (detects credit card numbers) and Social Security Numbers (US).

quotes: Zscaler provides the following predefined Data Loss Prevention (DLP) engines for higher accuracy in data classification and to reduce false positives.
| Credit Cards - predefined | Detects credit card numbers. |
| Social Security Numbers (US) - predefined | Detects US Social Security Numbers. |

uses-predefined.statement: The Understanding Data Classification page says DSPM uses predefined DLP engines and dictionaries for data classification.

quotes: DSPM uses predefined DLP engines and dictionaries for data classification

predefined-or-custom.title: Whether DSPM classifies with predefined engines only or custom engines too
predefined-or-custom.detail: The Understanding Data Classification page says "DSPM uses predefined DLP engines and dictionaries for data classification" while the settings page lists Engine Type as Predefined or Custom and the engines page says the service supports custom DLP engines. No capture says whether a custom engine classifies data in DSPM.

predefined-engine-list.title: The full predefined DLP engine list
predefined-engine-list.detail: The predefined engines page lists about 70 rows; only two are quoted as examples. The page title mentions dictionaries but only engines are listed.
